audits.claim_text: Plumvale Toonworks' AI pipeline cut per-episode costs by 40%.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: Our AI-assisted pipeline reduced per-episode costs by 40%.
Plumvale Toonworks said its AI-assisted pipeline cut per-episode costs by 40%.
supporting_evidence.summary: Trade report repeating the release (same group).

audits.explanation: DEMO: Both items trace to the studio's own release (one independence group); no cost breakdown or independent data. A source's existence does not prove its claim.
additional_research_needed: Request budget data or an independent producer account.

audits.claim_text: Plumvale is the first studio to deliver a full season using AI in-betweening.

contradicting_evidence.excerpt: Fernvale Pictures delivered a full season using AI in-betweening in 2024.
contradicting_evidence.summary: Archive documents an earlier studio doing the same.

audits.explanation: DEMO: The archive records Fernvale Pictures delivering a full AI in-betweened season in 2024, two years earlier, directly refuting the 'first' claim.

missing_fields.note: Claim made by reporter without citation.

audits.claim_text: In the survey, 58% of members said their hours had fallen since AI tools were introduced.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: 58% of responding members reported fewer paid hours since AI tools were introduced (n=1,200).
supporting_evidence.summary: Primary survey document confirms the figure.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: In the survey, 58% of members said their hours had fallen since AI tools were introduced.
In the survey, 58% of members said their hours had fallen since AI tools were introduced.
supporting_evidence.summary: Syndicated copy — same group as wire report.

audits.explanation: DEMO: Confirmed against the primary survey. The wire story and its syndicated copy share one group (grp_demo_wire_story) and add no independent confirmation. Verified means the survey reported this — not that hours fell by that amount.

audits.claim_text: AI tools are the main cause of falling animation employment in the region.

supporting_evidence.summary: Union survey attributes hour losses to AI (self-reported).

contradicting_evidence.excerpt: Animation employment declined 6% year over year; average crew size declined 9%.
contradicting_evidence.summary: Official data show decline but do not attribute cause; bulletin lists production volume as a factor (fictional).

audits.explanation: DEMO: Decline is documented, but causation is contested: the union attributes it to AI, official data do not attribute a cause.

confidence.rationale: Causal claim with no causal analysis.

additional_research_needed: Seek causal analysis separating AI adoption from production volume.

audits.claim_text: Independent animation output will double by 2028.
audits.explanation: DEMO: A prediction about 2028; it cannot be verified now and no supporting projection is cited.

audits.claim_text: Animation crews in the region have shrunk by about a fifth.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: Animation employment declined 6% year over year; average crew size declined 9%.
supporting_evidence.summary: Official data confirm crews shrank, but by 9%, not about 20%.

audits.explanation: DEMO: The direction (smaller crews) is supported by official data; the magnitude ('about a fifth') is overstated — the bulletin reports 9%.

confidence.rationale: Official dataset, but regional aggregate and one quarter only.

executive_summary.text: [DEMO] Fictional coverage shows a studio claiming large AI cost savings (Unverified/Partially Supported), a union survey reporting fewer hours (Verified as reported), a 'first studio' claim that is Contradicted, a causal claim that is Disputed, and an Unverified prediction.

key_findings.statement: [DEMO] The fictional union survey reported that 58% of responding members had fewer paid hours since AI tools arrived (Verified as a report of the survey result, not of the size of the loss).
[DEMO] Regional crews shrank, but by 9% rather than 'about a fifth' (Partially Supported); whether AI is the main cause of falling employment is Disputed.
[DEMO] The fictional studio's 40% cost-saving claim and the columnist's 2028 forecast are Unverified, and the studio's 'first' claim is Contradicted by an archive record.
